instructions: Present these sketches during onboarding taste profile. Each sketch is a concrete, vivid one-liner about a real Buffalo date scenario. After collecting reactions, run the inference algorithm in SKILL.md to derive preferences.

sketches.sketch: Renting bikes at the Outer Harbor and riding the waterfront trail along Lake Erie — an hour of moving around with the city skyline behind you, then food trucks in Larkinville
Shea's Performing Arts for a Broadway touring show — the 1926 theater itself is stunning, and a pre-show dinner somewhere on Main Street before curtain
An afternoon at the Buffalo AKG Art Museum — one of the best modern art collections in the country — then wandering Elmwood Village for coffee, maybe a bookstore, dinner at whatever looks good
Canalside on a summer evening — outdoor concert, cold beers, the Erie Canal lit up, hanging out with a thousand other people all in a good mood
Delaware Park on a Sunday morning — walking the Olmsted-designed paths around Hoyt Lake, coffee from somewhere nearby, no particular agenda
Buffalo Sabres game at KeyBank Center — hockey is fast and genuinely fun even if you don't follow the sport, and the downtown arena makes it easy to grab dinner before or after
Tifft Nature Preserve — 264 acres of urban wetlands right in the city, birdwatching if you're into it, genuinely quiet trails and surprisingly wild for being inside Buffalo
Dinner at the Rooftop at Hotel Henry — the old 19th-century psychiatric asylum turned boutique hotel, cocktails and dinner in one of the most architecturally striking buildings in the state
A full Saturday eating your way through Buffalo — farmers market in the morning, a couple of food stops through the afternoon, a proper dinner at night
Day trip to Niagara Falls — Maid of the Mist boat right into the mist, genuinely one of the most dramatic things you can do within 30 minutes of Buffalo
A show at a small local venue — a band you've never heard of or a touring act, standing room, loud and energetic, out by midnight
An Elmwood Village afternoon — good coffee, browsing an independent bookstore, window shopping, stopping for dinner whenever you get hungry
